analyze_document.title: Submit a document for analysis
analyze_document.description:
Start analysing a document with a prebuilt or custom model. Returns 202 and NOT the result -- the analysis runs asynchronously and get_analyze_result fetches it once done.
Pass the document as `url_source` (a publicly reachable URL, or a blob URL with a SAS token) or `base64_source`. A URL is cheaper for anything large.
Model choice decides what you get back. `prebuilt-read` gives text. `prebuilt-layout` adds tables, selection marks and reading order, and with `output_content_format` set to `markdown` returns the whole document as Markdown with tables preserved -- which is what you want for feeding a language model. `prebuilt-invoice` and its siblings return typed fields instead.
`pages` limits the work to a range like "1-5", which matters on a 200-page PDF. `features` enables extras that cost more, such as `ocrHighResolution` for small print or `keyValuePairs`.
analyze_document.notes: Returns 202 with the result id in an Operation-Location header this package does not surface. Poll get_analyze_result.

model_id.description: The model to analyse with -- prebuilt-read, prebuilt-layout, prebuilt-invoice, prebuilt-receipt, prebuilt-idDocument, or a custom model id from list_models.

url_source.description: A publicly reachable URL to the document, or a blob URL with a SAS token. Use this or base64_source.

base64_source.description: The document as a base64 string. Use this or url_source.

pages.description: Page range to analyse, e.g. "1-5" or "1,3,5-7". Omit for the whole document. Worth setting on anything long.

locale.description: Document locale hint, e.g. "en-US". Improves accuracy where the language is known.

output_content_format.description: text returns plain content; markdown returns the document as Markdown with tables and headings intact, which is what to use for RAG.

string_index_type.description: How character offsets in the result are counted.

features.description: Optional add-on capabilities, e.g. ocrHighResolution, formulas, styleFont, barcodes, languages or keyValuePairs. Each costs extra.

output.description: Empty body. The result id is in the Operation-Location response header.

get_analyze_result.title: Get the result of a document analysis
get_analyze_result.description:
Fetch an analysis submitted by analyze_document. `status` is `notStarted`, `running`, `succeeded` or `failed` -- poll until it settles, which takes seconds for a page and tens of seconds for a long PDF.
On success, `analyzeResult` holds the extraction: `content` is the whole document as text (or Markdown, if that was asked for), `pages` the per-page words and lines with their bounding boxes, `tables` the extracted tables cell by cell, and `documents` the typed fields when a prebuilt or custom model produced them.
Each field carries a `confidence`. Treat anything below about 0.8 as needing a human, particularly on invoice totals and identity documents.

model_id.description: The model the analysis was submitted to.

result_id.description: The analysis id, the GUID at the end of the Operation-Location header analyze_document returned.

output.description: The analysis, or its progress while still running.

analyzeResult.description: content, pages, tables, paragraphs, styles and documents with their typed fields and confidences.

list_models.title: List the models available on this resource
list_models.description: Every document model this resource can analyse with -- the prebuilt ones Azure ships and any custom models built here -- with each one's description and creation date. The ids are what analyze_document's `model_id` takes.

output.description: The models available on the resource.

items.description: modelId, description, createdDateTime, expirationDateTime and apiVersion.

get_model.title: Get a model and the fields it extracts
get_model.description:
One model in detail, including `docTypes` -- the document types it recognises and, for each, the exact field schema it will return. This is how you find out what to expect from a prebuilt model's output without running it on a document first.
For a custom model it also reports the training accuracy per field, which is the honest measure of whether it is ready for use.

output.description: The model and its field schema.

docTypes.description: Each document type with its fieldSchema and, for custom models, fieldConfidence.

build_model.title: Train a custom document model
build_model.description:
Build a custom model from labelled documents in an Azure Blob Storage container. There is no upload here -- `container_url` must be a blob container URL WITH a SAS token granting read and list, and the labelling files have to be in it already, which normally means using Document Intelligence Studio first.
`build_mode` decides the approach: `template` learns fixed positions and needs about five documents of a consistent layout; `neural` handles varying layouts and structured text, takes longer to train, and is what you want for documents that are not all laid out the same way.
Training is asynchronous -- watch it with get_operation. Reusing an existing model_id fails, so build a new id and switch over.
build_model.notes: Training runs asynchronously and is billed. The container URL must include a SAS token.

model_id.description: An id for the new model. Must not already exist.

build_mode.description: template for consistent layouts, neural for varying ones. Neural trains more slowly and generalises better.

container_url.description: Blob container URL containing the labelled training set, INCLUDING a SAS token with read and list permission.

prefix.description: Only use blobs under this path prefix within the container.

tags.description: Tags to store on the model.

output.description: Empty. Training runs asynchronously -- follow it with get_operation.

delete_model.title: Delete a custom model
delete_model.description:
Remove a custom model. Irreversible -- the trained model is gone, and rebuilding it needs the original labelled training set. Anything calling analyze_document with that model id starts failing immediately.
Prebuilt models cannot be deleted.
delete_model.notes: Irreversible. Rebuilding requires the original labelled training data.

list_classifiers.title: List custom document classifiers
list_classifiers.description: The document classifiers built on this resource. A classifier sorts an incoming document into a category -- invoice, contract, form -- so a pipeline can then route it to the right extraction model. Useful in front of analyze_document when the incoming documents are mixed.

classify_document.title: Submit a document for classification
classify_document.description:
Sort a document into one of a classifier's categories, and optionally split a multi-document PDF into its constituent documents.
Asynchronous like analyze_document: returns 202 with the result id in an Operation-Location header this package does not surface, and the result is fetched with get_classify_result.
`split` set to `auto` finds the boundaries between documents in one PDF, which is how a scanned batch is separated before each part is analysed.
classify_document.notes: Returns 202 with the result id in a header this package does not surface. Poll get_classify_result.

classifier_id.description: The classifier to use, from list_classifiers.

url_source.description: A publicly reachable URL to the document, or a blob URL with a SAS token.

base64_source.description: The document as a base64 string. Use this or url_source.

split.description: auto splits a multi-document file into parts; none treats the whole file as one document; perPage classifies each page separately.

output.description: Empty body. The result id is in the Operation-Location response header.

get_classify_result.title: Get the result of a document classification
get_classify_result.description: Fetch a classification submitted by classify_document. `status` reaches `succeeded` when done, and `analyzeResult.documents` then holds one entry per detected document with its `docType`, `confidence` and the page range it spans -- which is what you feed into per-document analyze_document calls when splitting a batch.

classifier_id.description: The classifier the document was submitted to.

result_id.description: The classification id from the Operation-Location header.

output.description: The classification, or its progress while still running.

analyzeResult.description: documents, each with docType, confidence and the pages it covers.

list_operations.title: List recent long-running operations
list_operations.description:
Model builds, copies and composes started on this resource in the last 24 hours, each with its id, kind, status and percent complete.
This is also the practical way to recover an operation id when the `Operation-Location` header was not captured -- the entries here carry the ids that get_operation takes.

items.description: operationId, kind, status, percentCompleted, createdDateTime and resourceLocation.

get_operation.title: Get the status of a long-running operation
get_operation.description:
Follow a model build, copy or compose: `status` moves through `notStarted`, `running` and then `succeeded` or `failed`, with `percentCompleted` in between. On failure the `error` object says why -- usually a labelling problem or a container the SAS token could not read.
This is how you know a build_model call has finished; there is no notification.

operation_id.description: The operation id, from list_operations or an Operation-Location header.

status.description: notStarted, running, succeeded, failed or canceled.

get_resource_info.title: Get the resource's model quota
get_resource_info.description: How many custom models this resource holds against the limit it is allowed -- 5000 on a standard tier, 500 on free. A build_model that fails with a quota error is explained here, and the fix is to delete models that are no longer used.

output.description: The resource's custom model quota and usage.
